text:
sophia: Ran an nsys + perfetto sampling run on 8xA100 w/ the kernel-selector v2 patch applied. seeing unexpected gaps in the timeline during KV handshake; suspect scheduler is forcing extra stream syncs. attaching quick notes and timeline link.

raj: can you paste the exact nsys cmd you used? want to reproduce locally.

sophia: nsys profile --sample=cpu,mem --trace=cuda,osrt --output=nsys_kv_v2 ./run_inference.sh --batch 4 --tp 2
I captured perfetto and a small nvprof snapshot too. perfetto UI: https://perfetto.dev/trace/viewer?xyz (redacted)

mike: quick glance: NCCL shows send/recv tails overlapping with cudaMemcpyAsync on stream 3. are we accidentally serializing the completion callback? :thinking:

sophia: yeah that's what I thought — the selector added an exclusive per-request R/W stream when KV miss occurs. When a req hits KV miss on rank 0, other ranks wait on the barrier. timeline snippet:

```
GPU0: kernelA -> cudaMemcpyAsync(host) -> ncclSend -> idle -> kernelB
GPU1: kernelA -> ncclRecv -> kernelB -> ncclAllreduce
```
The idle between send and kernelB is ~2.3ms and corresponds to a cudaStreamSynchronize in our request path.

perf-bot: nsys summary attached: kernel_launchs: 12.3k, cudaMemcpy: 1.1k, blocking_syncs: 24 (up from 6 baseline)

eva: were these blocking syncs introduced by the batching heuristic change last week? we changed the heuristic to flush small batches on KV miss to reduce latency for short prompts.

sophia: yes the heuristic calls flush_and_wait() for tiny partial batches to avoid head-of-line blocking, but that flush forces a host-side sync on the NVTX marker used by the scheduler.

raj: thoughts on mitigation? maybe change flush to async memcpy + signal, or let the kernel-selector pick a non-blocking path for known KV miss pattern.

mike: two practical options: 1) keep flush but move it to a dedicated non-blocking stream and use event-based wait on GPU (cudaEventRecord + cudaStreamWaitEvent) so we avoid host sync; 2) change batching heuristic to prefer filling up to at least 2 tokens before flush when TP>1 so frequency of KV misses drops.

sophia: I prototyped option 1 — replaced host sync with cudaEvent-based fence and nsys shows blocked_syncs drop to 3, tail idle almost gone. throughput +12% on 4xTP job. attaching short perfetto clip: https://perfetto.dev/trace/viewer?abc (redacted)

eva: awesome. any regression risk? event-based waits can hide real ordering bugs. need a canary on staging 8xA100 for 24h. also add a unit test exercising concurrent KV miss across ranks.

sophia: agreed. will open a PR with patch + regression test. notes in PR: use cudaEvent with flags=0, ensure event recorded on the producer stream right after memcpy, consumer stream waits via cudaStreamWaitEvent; fallback to host sync if event API returns resource error.

raj: also capture NCCL timelines with NET=nvidia fabric on to ensure no unexpected network retries. i saw a 1% burst of retransmits on one run.

mike: yay, thanks. can you include an nsight capture for an offending run? helps to see kernel scheduling on each GPU lane.

sophia: will do. planning: 1) open PR for event-fence fix, 2) canary deploy on staging (24h), 3) collect nsight/ perfetto + NCCL logs to validate. pinging @perf-bot to schedule nightly runs for 48h. :eyes:
